For example, the corpuscular theory of matter cannot be true, according to Berkeley, because there is nothing for it to be true of.

zh: 贝克莱拒绝了牛顿的万有引力理论，因为该理论试图通过“物体的原因”来解释事物。这自然不难理解：既然太阳和月亮作为物质具有质量，而我对它们的感官印象却毫无质量可言，因此只能对我的想象力产生引力作用。他同样不认同有史以来最重要的数学发现——微积分，若没有微积分，现代科学的成就便无从谈起。但这无妨。由于“真实空间”可无限分割的概念与他的哲学基本公设相悖，他对此进行了猛烈抨击。在与当时的主要科学发现针锋相对之后，贝克莱晚年致力于颂扬焦油水的特性，将其奉为能治愈一切疾病的灵丹妙药。人们或许会认为，如此离奇的哲学思想理应销声匿迹。
en: Berkeley rejected Newton’s theory of gravity, because it attempted to explain things by “corporeal causes.” Naturally enough, since, while the sun and moon, being material, have mass, my sense-impressions of these have none whatsoever and can exercise a gravitational pull only on my imagination. He likewise disapproved of the most important mathematical discovery of all – the differential and integral calculus, without which the achievements of modern science would not have been possible. But no matter. Since the concept of infinite divisibility of “real space” ran counter to the basic postulates of his philosophy, he opposed it vehemently. Having set his face against the major scientific discoveries of his day, Berkeley spent his later years extolling the properties of tar-water as an elixir to cure all ills. One could be excused for thinking that such an eccentric philosophy as this would vanish without trace.

zh: 事实并非如此。贝克莱主教的思想至今仍对资产阶级哲学家产生着一种奇特的吸引力，它是逻辑实证主义和语言哲学中认识论的真正起源和基础。列宁在其著作《唯物主义与经验批判主义》中对此进行了精辟的论述，我们稍后将再次提及。
en: Not so. The ideas of Bishop Berkeley have continued to exercise a strange fascination on bourgeois philosophers down to the present day, being the true origin and basis of the theory of knowledge (‘epistemology’) of logical positivism and linguistic philosophy. This was dealt with brilliantly by Lenin in his book Materialism and Empirio-Criticism, to which we shall return later.

zh: 尽管听起来难以置信，但这种彻头彻尾的非理性、反科学的哲学，却通过逻辑实证主义以各种形式渗透到了许多科学家的思想中。在贝克莱在世时，他的思想并未引起多大反响。这些思想不得不等到我们这个充满矛盾的时代——人类知识的最大进步与最原始的文化倒退并存——才得以在体面社会中被接受。正如G.J. 沃诺克在《人类知识原理》序言中所指出的，贝克莱的哲学“在当今时代获得了比以往任何时候都更广泛的支持”。因此，“如今一些物理学家……倾向于像他一样论证，物理理论并非关乎事实真相，而本质上关乎数学和预测上的便利。”
科学家兼唯心主义哲学家爱丁顿曾宣称，我们：
en: Incredible as it may seem, this thoroughly irrational and anti-scientific philosophy has penetrated the thinking of many scientists, through the agency of logical positivism in different guises. In Berkeley’s lifetime his ideas did not get much of an echo. They had to wait for the intellectual climate of our own contradictory times, when the greatest advances of human knowledge rub shoulders with the most primitive cultural throwbacks to get accepted in polite society. As G. J. Warnock points out, in the introduction to The Principles of Human Knowledge, Berkeley’s philosophy “in our own day has won far more general support than ever before.” Thus, “today some physicists…are inclined to argue exactly as he did, that physical theory is not a matter of factual truth, but essentially of mathematical and predictive convenience.”
The scientist and idealist philosopher Eddington claimed that we:

zh: 有权相信，例如，存在他人能看见而我们自己看不见的颜色，他人感受到的牙痛，他人享受的快乐和忍受的痛苦等等，但我们无权推断那些无人经历且不构成任何“心灵”一部分的事件。
en: [H]ave a right to believe that there are, for instance, colours seen by other people but not by ourselves, toothaches felt by other people, pleasures enjoyed and pains endured by other people, and so on, but that we have no right to infer events experienced by no one and not forming part of any ‘mind’.

zh: 像A. J. 艾耶尔这样的逻辑实证主义者接受这样一种论点：我们只能认识“感觉内容”，因此关于物质世界是否存在的问题是“无意义的”。诸如此类。老贝克莱在坟墓里肯定笑翻了！
en: Logical positivists like A. J. Ayer accept the argument that we can only know “sense-contents” and, therefore, the question as to the existence of the material world is ‘meaningless’. And so on and so forth. Old Berkeley must be laughing in his grave!

zh: 任何理论或假说的价值，归根结底取决于它能否成功地应用于现实，能否增进我们对世界的认识以及对我们生活的掌控。一个无法做到这些的假说毫无用处，只是无谓的空想产物，就像中世纪经院哲学家们关于“针头上能有多少个天使跳舞”的争论一样。大学里浪费了大量时间，无休止地争论这类问题。就连伯特兰·罗素也不得不承认，像贝克莱那样的理论——“会禁止我们谈论任何我们自己没有明确察觉到的东西。如果是这样，这是一种在实践中无人能坚持的观点，而对于一个以实践为依据的理论来说，这是一种缺陷。”然而，紧接着下一句，他却不得不补充道：“关于验证的整个问题及其与知识的联系，既困难又复杂；因此，目前我将暂且搁置这一问题。”
这些问题之所以“困难又复杂”，只是对于那些接受“我们所能知道的仅限于感觉材料，且这些数据与物质世界相互分离、彼此独立”这一前提的人而言。既然这是许多现代哲学家的出发点，无论他们如何狡辩，都无法从贝克莱主教设下的陷阱中脱身。
en: The value of any theory or hypothesis is ultimately determined by whether it can be applied successfully to reality, whether it enhances our knowledge of the world and our control over our lives. A hypothesis which does none of these things is good for nothing, the product of idle speculation, like the disputations of the mediaeval Schoolmen about how many angels can dance on the head of a pin. A colossal amount of time has been wasted in universities on endlessly debating this kind of thing. Even Bertrand Russell is compelled to admit that a theory like Berkeley’s – “would forbid us to speak about anything that we have not ourselves explicitly noticed. If so, it is a view that no one can hold in practice, which is a defect in a theory that is advocated on practical grounds.” Yet in the very next sentence he feels obliged to add that “The whole question of verification, and its connection with knowledge, is difficult and complex; I will, therefore, leave it on one side for the present.”

These questions are only “difficult and complex” for someone who accepts the premise that all we can know are sense-data, separate and apart from the material world. Since this is the starting point of a great deal of modern philosophers, no matter how they twist and turn, they cannot dig themselves out of the trap set by Bishop Berkeley.

zh: 走投无路
en: THE END OF THE ROAD

zh: 经验主义哲学最初曾寄予厚望，但最终在大卫·休谟（1711—1776）手中戛然而止。作为一名铁杆托利党人，休谟忠实地遵循了贝克莱开辟的道路，尽管他走得更为谨慎。他的最著名著作《人性论》于1739 年在法国出版，却反响平平。对休谟而言，现实仅仅是一串印象的串联，其成因既未知亦不可知。他认为世界是否存在是一个无解之谜，并成为首批将这种无知用希腊语表述、称之为“不可知论”的哲学家之一。本质上，这是一种对古希腊怀疑论者“世界不可知”观点的倒退。
en: The philosophy of empiricism, which began its life with such great expectations, finally comes to a dead stop with David Hume (1711-76). An arch-Tory, Hume followed faithfully in the path laid down by Berkeley, albeit more cautiously. His most famous work, the Treatise on Human Nature was published in 1739 in France where it went down like a lead balloon. For Hume, reality is only a string of impressions, the causes of which are unknown and unknowable. He regarded the question of the existence or non-existence of the world to be an insoluble problem, and was one of the first of those philosophers to translate their ignorance into Greek and call it agnosticism. In essence, what we have here is a throwback to the idea of the Greek sceptics that the world is unknowable.

zh: 他之所以闻名于世，主要归功于其著作中题为《论知识与概率》的一章。在这方面，他同样缺乏原创性，只是进一步发展了贝克莱早已提出的观点，即因果关系并不存在。他反驳当时新兴的力学科学的发现，试图证明机械因果关系并不存在，我们不能说某一特定事件导致了另一事件，而只能说一事件紧随另一事件之后。因此，如果我们将一壶水烧至100 摄氏度，我们不能说这一行为导致了水沸腾，而只能说水在我们加热之后沸腾了。或者，如果一个人被一辆十吨重的卡车撞倒，我们无权断言他的死亡是由卡车造成的。死亡只是在时间上紧随其后发生，仅此而已。
en: His main claim to fame rests on the section of his work entitled Of Knowledge and Probability. Here also he was not original, but merely developed an idea already present in Berkeley, namely the non-existence of causation. Arguing against the discoveries of the newly developed science of mechanics, he tried to show that mechanical causation did not exist, that we cannot say that a particular event causes another event, but only that one event follows another. Thus, if we boil a kettle of water to 100 degrees centigrade, we cannot say that this action has caused it to boil, but only that the water boiled after we heated it. Or if a man is knocked over by a ten-ton truck, we have no right to affirm that his death was caused by this. It just succeeded it in time. That is all.

zh: 这听起来难以置信吗？但这正是严格应用此类狭隘经验主义的必然结果——这种经验主义要求我们“只看事实，仅看事实”。我们所能说的，仅仅是某个事实紧随另一个事实之后。我们无权断言一件事物确实导致了另一件事物，因为这将超出我们双眼和双耳在特定时刻所记录的单一事实。这一切不禁让人想起古哲人赫拉克利特的警告：“如果人的灵魂无法理解感官的语言，那么眼睛和耳朵对人来说就是糟糕的见证者。”
en: Does this seem incredible? But it is the inevitable result of the strict application of this kind of narrow empiricism, which demands of us that we stick to ‘the facts, and nothing but the facts.’ All we can say is that one fact follows another. We have no right to assert that one thing actually causes another, since this would be to go beyond the single fact registered by our eyes and ears at a given moment in time. All of which forcibly brings to mind the warning of old Heraclitus: “Eyes and ears are bad witnesses to men if they have souls that understand not their language.”

zh: 再次令人惊讶的是，在过去两个多世纪所产生的所有奇妙哲学思想中，现代哲学家和科学家竟然选择将……休谟的著作作为他们的出发点和灵感来源！他对于因果关系的否定，被人们热切地拿来作为某种意识形态支撑，以佐证海森堡等人试图从量子力学中得出的某些错误哲学结论。我们稍后将对此进行讨论。本质上，休谟主张，当我们说“A”导致“B”时，我们只是指这两件事在过去曾多次同时出现，因此我们相信它们未来可能会再次发生。然而，这并非确定性，而仅仅是一种信念。这不是必然性，而仅仅是概率。因此，“必然是存在于思想中的，而非存在于事物本身。”
en: Once again, it is astonishing to note that, of all the marvellous philosophical ideas produced in the last two centuries or so, modern philosophers and scientists choose to take as their starting-point and inspiration the writings of…Hume! His denial of causality has been eagerly seized upon in order to provide some ideological support for certain incorrect philosophical conclusions which Heisenberg and others have attempted to draw from quantum mechanics. We shall speak of that later. In essence, Hume asserts that, when we say ‘A’ causes ‘B’, we only mean that these two acts have been seen together many times in the past, and that, therefore, we believe they may be repeated in the future. This, however, is not a certainty but only a belief. It is not necessity, but only probability. Thus, “necessity is something that exists in the mind, not in objects.”

zh: 首先，否认因果关系会使我们进而否认科学和理性思维本身。科学的全部基础和存在意义，就在于试图对观察到的自然现象给出合理的解释。通过对大量事实的观察，我们得出一般性结论；如果这些结论经过充分检验并被证明具有广泛适用性，就会升华为科学定律。当然，所有这些定律都反映了人类发展特定阶段上的知识水平，因此，随后会被能够更好地解释事物的其他理论和假说所取代。在此过程中，我们对自然和自身都逐渐有了更深刻的理解。这一过程如同自然本身一样无边无际。因此，寻找能够解释一切的“绝对真理”，或者用时下流行的说法，寻找“普遍大理论”（Grand Universal Theory，GUT），其成效大概与寻找“哲学家之石”相差无几。
en: First of all, to deny causation leads us to the denial of scientific and rational thought in general. The whole basis and raison d’être of science is the attempt to provide a rational explanation for the observed phenomena of nature. From the observation of a large number of facts, we draw general conclusions, which, if they have been sufficiently tested and shown to have a wide application, acquire the status of scientific laws. Naturally, all such laws reflect the state of our knowledge at a given stage of human development, and, consequently, are subsequently overtaken by other theories and hypotheses, which explain things better. In the process, we gradually arrive at a deeper understanding both of nature and ourselves. This process is as limitless as nature itself. Thus, to look for an Absolute Truth, which would explain everything, or, to use a fashionable expression, a Grand Universal Theory (GUT) is about as profitable as looking for the philosopher’s stone.
body.review: 原文将GUT展开为Grand Universal Theory，译文据此保留；通常物理学缩写GUT对应Grand Unified Theory（大统一理论），二者不应静默混同。

zh: 某项概括在特定时刻可能被证伪，并不意味着我们可以完全摒弃概括。这也不意味着我们必须放弃对客观真理的探索，而去寻求像休谟那样的怀疑论立场——这种立场因其与我们的实际实践——无论是科学还是日常生活——完全无关，实际上不过是一种故作高深的姿态。这是一种愚蠢的做作，就像那些否认物质世界存在的人一样：他们虽持此观点，却并未因此停止饮食；他们虽坚称因果关系不存在，却会非常小心，避免在不恰当的时刻与十吨卡车发生物理碰撞。
en: The fact that a particular generalisation may be falsified at a given moment does not entitle us to dispense with generalisations altogether. Nor does it mean that we have to renounce the search for objective truth, taking refuge in a sceptical attitude like that of Hume, which, because of its complete and utter irrelevance to our actual practice, whether in science or in everyday life, is really just a pretentious pose. It is an idiotic posing, like that of those who deny the existence of the material world, but who do not, on that account, refrain from eating and drinking, and who, while firmly maintaining the non-existence of causality, are very careful to avoid untimely physical encounters with ten-ton trucks.

zh: 所有自然法则都基于因果关系。海洋潮汐是由太阳和月亮的引力引起的。原子裂变会引发核爆炸。长期缺乏食物和饮水会导致死亡，而被卡车碾压则是以另一种方式导致了同样的结果。在这个充满罪恶的物质世界里，因果关系的存在是再确定不过的了。但这对休谟的追随者来说仍不够确定。若采纳他的论证思路，所有未来预测都将变得不合逻辑，因为事情总有可能出现不同的结果。伯特兰·罗素据称一本正经地解释道：
en: All natural laws are based on causality. The ocean tides are caused by the gravitational pull of the sun and moon. The splitting of the atom causes a nuclear explosion. Deprivation of food and drink over a long period causes death, and being run over by a lorry causes the same result by other means. The existence of causality is as certain as anything can be in this sinful material world of ours. But it is not certain enough for the disciples of Hume. Accepting his line of argument, all future prediction becomes irrational, because there is always the possibility that things will turn out differently. Bertrand Russell, supposedly with a straight face, explains:

zh: 我的意思是，即便是我们最坚定的预期——例如明天太阳会升起——也没有丝毫理由认为其实现的可能性比不实现的可能性更大。
en: I mean that, taking even our firmest expectations, such as that the sun will rise tomorrow, there is not a shadow of reason for supposing them more likely to be verified than not.

zh: 随后他进一步指出：
en: Further on he says:

zh: 例如：（重申前文的比喻）当我看到一个苹果时，过往的经验使我预期它尝起来会像苹果，而不是烤牛肉；但这种预期没有任何理性的依据。
en: For example: when (to repeat a former illustration) I see an apple, past experience makes me expect that it will taste like an apple, and not like roast beef; but there is no rational justification for this expectation.

zh: 根据休谟的观点，既然我们无法确知任何事物，他便得出结论：“我们关于因果关系的全部推理，无非源于习惯；而且信念更准确地说是我们本性中感性部分的行为，而非理性部分的行为。”
换言之，知识被摒弃，取而代之的是信念。
en: Since we cannot know anything, according to Hume, he concludes that “all our reasonings concerning causes and effects, are derived from nothing but custom; and that belief is more properly an act of the sensitive, than of the cogitative part of our natures.”
In other words, knowledge is abandoned in favour of belief.

zh: 应该牢记的是，所有这些的明确意图是消除思想中的形而上学，从而将思想限制在对“事实”的简单且（希望是）科学的罗列上。曾有位机智之士将形而上学定义为“一个盲人在黑暗的房间里寻找一顶并不存在的黑帽子”。这句话恰如其分地描述了那些人的形而上学摸索——他们通过否认因果关系，立即为非理性敞开了大门。随着休谟的出现，经验哲学完成了一个完整的循环。正如罗素正确指出的：
en: It should be borne in mind that the declared intention of all this is to eliminate metaphysics from thought, which will thus be limited to a bare and, hopefully, scientific enumeration of the ‘facts’. Some wit once defined metaphysics as “a blind man, in a dark room, looking for a black hat which isn’t there.” This phrase adequately describes the metaphysical fumbling of those who, by denying causation, immediately open the door to irrationality. With Hume, empirical philosophy comes full circle. As Russell correctly says:

zh: 休谟对所谓“知识”的探究所得到的最终结果，并非我们所设想的他所期望的。他的著作副标题是：《尝试将实验推理方法引入道德领域》。显然，他起初相信科学方法能揭示真理、全部真理，且唯有真理；然而，他最终却确信，信念绝非理性，因为我们一无所知。在阐述了怀疑论的论据（第一卷，第四部分，第一节）之后，他继续论述，并非为了反驳这些论据，而是退而诉诸天生的轻信。
en: The ultimate outcome of Hume’s investigation of what passes for knowledge is not what we must suppose him to have desired. The sub-title of his book is: ‘An attempt to introduce the experimental method of reasoning into moral subjects.’ It is evident that he started out with a belief that scientific method yields the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth; he ended, however, with the conviction that belief is never rational, since we know nothing. After setting forth the arguments for scepticism (Book I, part IV, sec. I), he goes on, not to refute the arguments, but to fall back on natural credulity.

zh: 人们可能会忍不住问，这种哲学的实际价值何在。对此，休谟并未给出答案，他仅以一种极尽轻浮、略带玩世不恭的语气评论道：
en: One may be tempted to ask what the practical worth of such a philosophy is. On this point no answer is forthcoming from Hume, who comments with the utmost frivolity, tinged with cynicism:

zh: 这种针对理性和感官的怀疑，是一种病症，永远无法彻底治愈，无论我们如何驱散它，它都会时时卷土重来，即便我们有时似乎已经完全摆脱了它……唯有漫不经心和心不在焉才能为我们提供任何解药。正因如此，我完全依赖它们；并且理所当然地认为，无论读者此刻持何种观点，一小时后他都会被说服，相信既存在外部世界，也存在内部世界。
en: This sceptical doubt, both with respect to reason and the senses, is a malady, which can never be radically cured, but must return upon us every moment, however we may chase it away, and sometimes may seem entirely free from it … Carelessness and inattention alone can afford us any remedy. For this reason I rely entirely upon them; and take it for granted, whatever may be the reader’s opinion at this present moment, that an hour hence he will be persuaded there is both an external and internal world.

zh: 这并非真正的哲学，而恰恰是一个形而上学的死胡同。它既未能向我们揭示任何关于世界的事实，也无法引领我们走向任何地方。这正是人们对一个认为“学习哲学除了作为一种消遣时光的愉快方式之外别无理由”的人所抱有的预期。事实上，学习休谟的哲学除了作为一种毫无意义的浪费时间的方式之外，确实没有任何理由。
en: This is not real philosophy but precisely a metaphysical dead end. It tells us nothing about the world and leads nowhere. Just what one would expect from a man who thought that there was no reason to study philosophy except as a pleasant way of passing the time. And indeed, there is certainly no reason to study Hume’s philosophy except as a pointless way of wasting time.

zh: 有一点我们可以认同伯特兰·罗素的观点：休谟的哲学“体现了十八世纪理性思想的破产。”

休谟的思想，如同贝克莱一样，代表着向主观唯心主义方向的转变。这是一种被彻底颠倒的经验主义。从“一切皆源于经验”这一出发点出发，我们得出的结论却是“无法从经验和观察中获得任何知识”。这与该时期伊始所秉持的进步科学精神背道而驰。从这种观点中无法获得任何积极的成果。因此，对于那些无法确信明天太阳还会升起的人，我们可以放心地让他们留在原地——留在黑暗之中，在那里，他们可以寄希望于某一天能吃到一个尝起来像烤牛肉的苹果，以此来缓解自己的困境。
en: On one thing we can agree with Bertrand Russell: the philosophy of Hume “represents the bankruptcy of eighteenth-century reasonableness.”

Hume’s ideas, like Berkeley’s, represent a move in the direction of subjective idealism. It is empiricism turned inside out. From the starting point that everything was learnt from experience, we arrive at the conclusion that nothing can be learnt from experience and observation. This is the antithesis of the progressive scientific spirit with which the period opened. Nothing positive can be obtained from such an outlook. We may therefore safely leave those who cannot be sure that the sun will rise tomorrow where we found them – in the dark, where they can find some consolation for their difficulties by looking forward one day to eating an apple which tastes like roast beef.

zh: 法国唯物主义的诞生
en: THE BIRTH OF FRENCH MATERIALISM

zh: 从这一刻起，英国哲学进一步发展的道路便被阻断了，但在那之前，它已为后来在法国被称为“启蒙运动”的思潮提供了强有力的推动力。人们有时将英国经验主义与法国唯物主义的差异归因于民族气质的不同。例如：
en: From this point on the road to further development of philosophy in Britain was blocked, but not before it had given a powerful impulse to the movement which became known as the Enlightenment in France. The difference between English empiricism and French materialism is sometimes ascribed to difference of national temperament. For instance:

zh: 将洛克的经验主义推向其最终归宿——即感觉主义和唯物主义——这是法国人承担的任务。尽管经验主义生长在英国原则的土壤上，并在那里很快普遍流行，但它绝不可能在英国发展成后来在法国显现的极端形式——即彻底摧毁道德和宗教生活的所有根基。这一最终结果与英国人的民族性格并不相符。
en: To carry out the empiricism of Locke into its ultimate consequence, into sensualism and materialism – this is the task which has been assumed by the French. Though grown on a soil of English principles, and very soon universally prevalent there, empiricism could not possibly be developed amongst the English into the extreme form which presently declared itself among the French – that is, into the complete destruction of all the foundations of the moral and religious life. This last consequence was not congenial to the national character of the English.

zh: 正如马克思和恩格斯在《神圣家族》中所指出的，不同民族的性情和传统无疑起到了重要作用：
en: The existence of different national temperaments and traditions undoubtedly played a major role, as Marx and Engels pointed out in The Holy Family:

zh: 法国唯物主义与英国唯物主义之间的差异，反映了两国之间的差异。法国人赋予了英国唯物主义机智、血肉和雄辩之辞。他们赋予了它原本所缺乏的气质与优雅。他们使它变得文明。
en: The difference between French and English materialism reflects the difference between the two nations. The French imparted to English materialism wit, flesh and blood, and eloquence. They gave it the temperament and grace that it lacked. They civilised it.

zh: 尽管如此，仅凭民族特性还不足以解释重大的历史运动。一百年前，法国人和英国人的性格也各不相同，却并未孕育出休谟或伏尔泰——他们是其所处时代的产物，或者更准确地说，是特定社会、经济和文化条件相互交织的产物。贝克莱和休谟的哲学诞生于资产阶级已经取得胜利、并试图平息革命的时期。孔多塞、狄德罗和伏尔泰则属于一个截然不同的时期——即通向1789—1793 年革命的社会与思想动荡时期。从一个重要意义上说，“哲学家们”反对宗教和正统思想的斗争，正是攻占巴士底狱的铺垫。事实上，在旧秩序被推翻之前，首先必须在人们心中证明它已然过时。
en: Nonetheless, to explain great historical movements it is not sufficient to appeal to national characteristics alone. The character of the French and English were also different 100 years before, without producing either Hume or Voltaire, who were products of their own time, or, more accurately, products of a particular concatenation of circumstances – social, economic and cultural. The philosophy of Berkeley and Hume emerged in a period when the bourgeoisie had already triumphed, and was trying to lay revolution to rest. Concordet, Diderot and Voltaire belong to an entirely different period – the period of social and intellectual ferment leading up to the revolution of 1789-93. In an important sense the struggle of the ‘philosophers’ against religion and orthodoxy was a preparation for the storming of the Bastille. Before the old order was overthrown in fact, it first had to be shown to be redundant in the minds of men and women.

zh: 普列汉诺夫在他那篇关于霍尔巴赫和爱尔维修的精彩论文中，曾这样论述十八世纪法国哲学：
en: In his excellent essay on Holbach and Helvétius, Plekhanov has this to say about eighteenth-century French philosophy:

zh: 十八世纪的唯物主义哲学是一种革命哲学。它仅仅是革命资产阶级反对神职人员、贵族和绝对君主制斗争的意识形态表现。不言而喻，在反对过时制度的斗争中，资产阶级不可能尊重那种从过去继承而来、并将该被鄙视的制度奉为神圣的世界观。“时代不同，形势不同，哲学也不同”，正如狄德罗在《百科全书》中关于霍布斯的条目中所精辟指出的那样。
en: Eighteenth-century materialist philosophy was a revolutionary philosophy. It was merely the ideological expression of the revolutionary bourgeoisie’s struggle against the clergy, the nobility, and the absolute monarchy. It goes without saying that, in its struggle against an obsolete system, the bourgeoisie could have no respect for a world-outlook that was inherited from the past and hallowed that despised system. “Different times, different circumstances, a different philosophy”, as Diderot so excellently put it in his article on Hobbes in the Encyclopédie.

zh: 洛克的思想对孔狄亚克神父（1715—1780）产生了巨大影响。孔狄亚克接受了洛克“一切知识源于感官”的学说，但更进一步主张，所有精神过程，甚至意志，都只是经过加工的感觉。他实际上从未否认上帝的存在，但仍然坚持认为只有物质才真实存在；对于一位神父来说，这是一个非常引人注目的结论。洛克的另一位门徒克劳德·阿德里安·爱尔维修（1715—1771），马克思曾说，正是通过他，“唯物主义才真正具有了法国特色。”
爱尔维修言辞如此直率，以至于连他的唯物主义同道们都感到震惊，不敢追随他得出那些大胆的结论。
en: The ideas of Locke had a great impact on the Abbe de Condillac (1715-80). Condillac accepted Locke’s teaching that all knowledge comes from the senses, but went even further, claiming that all mental processes, even the will, are only modified sensations. He never actually denied the existence of God, but nevertheless maintained that only matter existed; a very remarkable conclusion for someone who was a priest. Another disciple of Locke, Claude Adrien Helvétius (1715-71), with whom, said Marx, “materialism assumed a really French character.”
Helvétius was so outspoken that even his fellow materialists were taken aback, and did not dare follow him in his bold conclusions.

zh: 霍尔巴赫男爵（1723—1789）虽为德国人，但一生大部分时间都在法国度过，并在法国的唯物主义运动中发挥了重要作用。与爱尔维修一样，他也遭受了教会的迫害，其著作《自然体系》曾被巴黎高等法院下令公开焚毁。作为一位坚定的唯物主义者，霍尔巴赫抨击宗教和唯心主义，尤其是贝克莱的思想。洛克早已认为物质可能具有思维能力，霍尔巴赫对此表示热烈赞同，但与洛克不同的是，他准备将这一观点推向极致，将宗教和教会彻底抛弃：
en: Baron Holbach (1723-89), although a German, spent most of his life in France, where he played a major role in the materialist movement. Like Helvétius, he was persecuted by the Church, and his book Le Système de la Nature was publicly burnt by order of the Paris Parliament. A determined materialist, Holbach attacked religion and idealism, especially the ideas of Berkeley. Locke already thought it possible that matter could possess the faculty of thinking, and Holbach enthusiastically agreed, but, unlike Locke, was prepared to draw all the conclusions, throwing religion and the Church out of the window:

zh: 如果我们参考经验，就会发现，我们所见到的、无处不在、压倒全人类的种种灾祸的真正根源，就在于宗教的幻觉和观念之中。对自然原因的无知促使人类创造了神明；欺骗使这些神明变得可怕；对神明的有害观念一直困扰着人类，却并未使人类变得更好，反而让人们无谓地战栗，使他们的头脑充满幻象，阻碍了理性的进步，也妨碍了对幸福的追求。这些恐惧使人类沦为那些以关心其福祉为借口欺骗他们之人的奴隶；当被告知诸神要求他犯下罪行时，他便行恶；当被灌输诸神已将他判处于苦难之中时，他便在逆境中苟活；他从未敢反抗诸神或挣脱枷锁，因为人们不断向他灌输：愚昧、摒弃理性、精神麻木以及灵魂的屈辱，才是赢得永恒极乐的最佳途径。
en: If we consult experience, we shall see that it is in religious illusions and opinions that we should seek for the real source of the host of evils that we everywhere see overwhelming mankind. Ignorance of natural causes has led it to create its Gods; deception has made the latter terrible; a baneful concept of them has pursued man without making him any better, made him tremble uselessly, filled his mind with chimeras, opposing the progress of reason, and hindering the search for happiness. These fears have made him the slave of those who deceived him under the pretext of caring for his good; he did evil when he was told that his Gods called for crimes; he lived in adversity because he was made to hear that his Gods had condemned him to misery; he never dared to resist his Gods or to cast off his fetters, because it was drummed into him that stupidity, the renunciation of reason, spiritual torpor and abasement of the soul were the best means of winning eternal bliss.

zh: 拉美特利（1709—1751）更进一步指出，所有生命形式——无论是植物还是动物（包括人类）——都由以不同方式组织起来的物质构成。他的主要著作是著名的《人即机器》（L'Homme Machine）和《伊壁鸠鲁体系》（Le Système d'Epicure）。拉美特利在某种程度上是笛卡尔的追随者，后者曾指出，动物之所以是“机器”，是因为它们无法思考。拉美特利将此话字面理解，进而认为既然人与动物之间不存在质的区别，那么人同样也必须是机器。这仅仅反映了当时力学对科学思维的主导影响。
en: La Mettrie (1709-51) went still further in recognising that all forms of life, plant and animal (including man), consisted of matter organised in different ways. His main works were the famous L’Homme Machine (Man, a Machine), and Le Système d’Epicure (The System of Epicurus). La Mettrie was partly a follower of Descartes, who said that animals were machines in the sense that they could not think. Taking this literally, La Mettrie said that man also must be a machine, then, because there was no qualitative difference between man and the animals. This merely reflects the predominant influence of mechanics on the scientific thinking of the period.

zh: 拉美特利的意图是反对这样一种观点：即人类是上帝的特殊造物，凭借不朽灵魂这一特殊特权，与自然界的其他部分完全割裂开来。实际上，这一论点早已被英国唯物主义者兼科学家约瑟夫·普利斯特里驳斥，他如今主要以氧气的发现者而为人所知：
en: The intention of La Mettrie was to oppose the idea that man was a special creation of God, something entirely set aside from the rest of nature, by the special privilege of an immortal soul. This argument, in effect, was already disposed of by the English materialist and scientist Joseph Priestley, remembered today mainly as the discoverer of oxygen:

zh: 剃刀的切割能力取决于其组成部分之间的一种特定凝聚力及其排列方式。如果我们假设这把剃刀完全溶解在某种酸性溶液中，它的切割能力肯定会丧失或消失，尽管构成剃刀的金属颗粒在该过程中并未被消灭；而且在金属沉淀出来后，它的原有形状、切割能力等都可以恢复。因此，当身体因腐烂而溶解时，其思维能力便完全消失了。
en: The power of cutting, in a razor, depends upon a certain cohesion, and arrangement of the parts of which it consists. If we suppose this razor to be wholly dissolved in any acid liquor, its power of cutting will certainly be lost, or cease to be, though no particle of the metal that constituted the razor be annihilated by the process; and its former shape, and power of cutting, etc., may be restored to it after the metal has been precipitated. Thus when the body is dissolved by putrefaction, its power of thinking entirely ceases.

zh: 拉美特利认为，思维是物质的属性之一：
en: La Mettrie considered that thought was one of the properties of matter:

zh: 我认为思维与有组织的物质并不矛盾，以至于它似乎是后者的属性，正如电、运动能力、不可穿透性、广延等属性一样。
en: I believe thinking to be so little incompatible with organised matter that it seems to be a property of the latter in the same way as electricity, the faculty of movement, impenetrability, extent, etc.

zh: 从启蒙运动的激进唯物主义和理性主义出发，很容易得出革命性的结论，而人们也确实这样做了。伏尔泰（1694—1778），尽管并非真正的哲学家，但作为作家、历史学家和小册子作者，他在这一运动中发挥了重要作用。他因政治讽刺作品两次被捕，一生的大部分时间都不得不在法国境外度过。伏尔泰最伟大的贡献是他与狄德罗合作编纂的《百科全书》（1751—1780），这项浩大的工程系统地总结了当时的所有科学知识。众多最伟大的法国思想家参与了这项独一无二的任务：孟德斯鸠、卢梭、伏尔泰、霍尔巴赫、爱尔维修以及其他进步的唯物主义哲学家们齐心协力，共同创作了一部针对现有社会秩序的基础、其哲学和道德观的激进著作。
en: From the radical materialism and rationalism of the Enlightenment it was easy to draw revolutionary conclusions, and this was done. Voltaire (1694-1778), although not really a philosopher, played a prominent role in this movement as a writer, historian and pamphleteer. He was arrested twice for his political satires, and had to spend most of his life outside France. Voltaire’s greatest contribution was his collaboration with Diderot in the great Encyclopédie (1751-80), a massive undertaking which gave a systematic summary of all the scientific knowledge of the time. A galaxy of the greatest French thinkers participated in this unique task: Montesquieu, Rousseau, Voltaire, Holbach, Helvétius, and other progressive and materialist philosophers combined to produce a militant work directed against the basis of the existing social order, its philosophy and morality.

zh: 与法国唯物主义者的著作相比，让-雅克·卢梭的哲学观点代表了一种倒退。尽管如此，在社会批判领域，他创作了多部杰作，恩格斯特别点名赞扬了他的著作《论人类不平等的起源》。不过，由于他严格来说也不是一位真正的哲学家，我们在此就不深入探讨他的思想了。
en: Compared to the writings of the French materialists, the philosophical views of Jean-Jacques Rousseau represent a step backwards. Nevertheless, in the field of social criticism, he produced a number of masterpieces, and Engels specifically singled out for praise his work Discourse of the Origins of Inequality Among Men. Still, as he is also not really a philosopher in the strict sense, we will not enter into his ideas more fully here.

zh: 总体而言，这些作家为1789—1793 年的资产阶级革命铺平了道路。他们激烈的抨击矛头直指封建制度和教会的弊端。对他们中的大多数人来说，立宪君主制是理想的选择。尽管如此，不难看出，后来人们是如何从他们的著作中得出社会主义和共产主义结论的：
en: In general, these writers were preparing the ground for the bourgeois revolution of 1789-93. Their fierce denunciations are directed against the evils of feudalism and the Church. The ideal for most of them was a constitutional monarchy. Nevertheless, it is easy to see how, later on, people began to draw socialist and communist conclusions from their writings:

zh: 无需多深思即可从唯物主义的教义中看出：人类生而善良且智力天赋平等；经验、习惯和教育具有无上力量；环境对人的影响；工业的重大意义；享乐的正当性等等——由此可见，唯物主义与共产主义及社会主义之间有着必然的联系。如果人的所有知识、感觉等都源于感官世界及其中的经验，那么需要做的是这样安排经验世界：使人能够在其中体验并习惯于真正合乎人性的事物，并使人意识到自己作为人的存在。

如果正确理解的利益是所有道德的原则，那么就必须使人的私利与全人类的利益相一致。如果人在唯物主义意义上是不自由的，即自由并非源于避免这样或那样的消极能力，而是源于彰显其真正个性的积极能力，那么就不应通过惩罚个人来惩治犯罪，而必须摧毁犯罪的反社会根源，并赋予每个人在社会中充分展现其生命本质的空间。如果人是受环境塑造的，那么环境就必须变得人性化。如果人是受自然塑造的，他只有在社会中才能发展出自己的真实本性，而其本性的力量不应以孤立个体的力量来衡量，而应以社会的力量来衡量。
en: There is no need for any great penetration to see from the teaching of materialism on the original goodness and equal intellectual endowment of men, the omnipotence of experience, habit and education, and the influence of environment on man, the great significance of industry, the justification of enjoyment, etc., how necessarily materialism is connected with communism and socialism. If man draws all his knowledge, sensation, etc., from the world of the senses and the experience gained in it, then what has to be done is to arrange the empirical world in such a way that man experiences and becomes accustomed to what is truly human in it and that he becomes aware of himself as man.

If correctly understood interest is the principle of all morality, man’s private interest must be made to coincide with the interest of humanity. If man is unfree in the materialistic sense, i.e., is free not through the negative power to avoid this or that, but through the positive power to assert his true individuality, crime must not be punished in the individual, but the anti-social sources of crime must be destroyed, and each man must be given social scope for the vital manifestation of his being. If man is shaped by environment, his environment must be made human. If man is shaped by nature, he will develop his true nature only in society, and the power of his nature must be measured not by the power of the separate individual but by the power of society.
